topic: For every finite labelled causally sufficient linear Gaussian DAG with unrestricted positive noise variances and one coefficient per block of each target's parent partition, allowing singleton blocks, characterize equality of the full positive-definite covariance models. Prove that two blocked-colour states are equivalent exactly when they are connected by covered reversals whose reversed edge is a singleton block and whose endpoint partitions agree on their common parents, with the prescribed partition transport. Equivalently, prove the static criterion: common skeleton and unshielded colliders, identical nonsingleton parent-block families at every vertex, and fixed orientation for every edge joining vertices with unequal block families. Derive complete component enumeration, a shortest reversal path whose length is the number of disagreeing arrows, fixed-p generic Gaussian likelihood/BIC component recovery, and simultaneous inference for the component's finite causal-effect set. Do not broaden to unrestricted cross-target edge colourings or equate a compelled arrow with an identified coefficient. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Tangent supports at diagonal covariances recover each nonsingleton parent block; an exact sparse covariance separator forces every reversed edge to join equal endpoint block families; Chickering's monotone reversal theorem then supplies the proposed path. Exhaustive p=5 enumeration matched all 348631 states and 153462 static classes to move components, with exact separators and mixed-partition stress witnesses. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Independently audit tangent-support recovery and the arbitrary-reversed-edge sparse separator, especially extra target parents and simultaneous arrow changes, and verify the imported generic-faithfulness and monotone-transformation results. EARLY KILL TEST: Reproduce the exact separator on legal five-node pairs and audit the monotone induction; any full-model-equivalent pair with different nonsingleton blocks or a reversal across unequal endpoint families falsifies the theorem. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/eid_blocked_colour_reversal_complete.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize equality of full positive-definite covariance models for blocked edge-coloured linear Gaussian DAGs when singleton coefficient blocks are allowed.

source_refs.claim: Question 20 asks for a graphical characterization of edge-coloured DAG model equivalence and specifically flags reversible or recolourable edges.
source_refs.author: Tobias Boege, Kaie Kubjas, Pratik Misra, Liam Solus
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B

source_refs.claim: The paper completely characterizes distributional equivalence under groupwise equal error variances and gives a CPDAG representation, the closest vertex-constraint analogue.
source_refs.author: Jun Wu, Mathias Drton
source_refs.venue: IEEE Journal on Selected Areas in Information Theory

source_refs.claim: For ordinary DAGs, covered edge reversals generate every Markov-equivalent transformation and can reverse each disagreeing edge once.
source_refs.author: David Maxwell Chickering

open_problems.why_unsolved: Boege et al. prove structural identifiability for properly blocked coefficient colourings but expressly leave equivalence open once singleton or uncoloured edges are admitted. Singleton blocks restore some ordinary Markov-equivalent reversals, while nonsingleton within-target coefficient equalities forbid others. Neither the ordinary skeleton-and-unshielded-collider criterion nor the singleton-free theorem determines whether equality is exactly captured by invariant nonsingleton parent-block families, fixed arrows between unequal endpoint families, and partition-compatible covered reversals.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient static graphical criterion and an equivalent generating set of partition-transported covered reversals, including a shortest-path theorem, or a smallest legal counterexample to that proposed characterization.

writing_exemplar.why: It introduces the exact coefficient-coloured Gaussian DAG language and frames graphical and transformational equivalence as the central missing problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: ordinary Gaussian DAGs identify only a Markov class -> coefficient equalities refine observational models -> singleton-free blocked colourings can identify one DAG -> singleton blocks reopen a structured equivalence problem

method_exemplars.technique: Use rational recovery of structural coefficients, coloured Markov constraints, and smooth covariance-model geometry to turn model equality into graphical invariants.
method_exemplars.why_closest: These are the exact observable constraints whose invariance must yield the blocked static criterion.

method_exemplars.technique: Extract orientation restrictions induced by equality constraints and combine them with ordinary CPDAG orientation rules.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It solves the structurally analogous equivalence problem for equalities among error variances rather than within-target coefficients.

method_exemplars.technique: Use compatible-colouring least-squares decomposition and the associated MLE existence and uniqueness argument.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Blocked colourings are compatible, so a recovered component has the same local regression likelihood structure needed for an estimation rung.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether tangent supports at a diagonal covariance recover every nonsingleton within-target parent block in a blocked coefficient-coloured Gaussian DAG.

source_refs.claim: The coloured-DAG covariance image is a smooth algebraic manifold with a rationally identifiable parametrization, but no diagonal tangent-support reconstruction of blocks is given.
source_refs.author: Tobias Boege, Kaie Kubjas, Pratik Misra, Liam Solus
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B

source_refs.claim: RDAG models have explicit equality-constrained likelihood geometry and MLE conditions, but the paper does not reconstruct coefficient blocks from tangent signatures.
source_refs.author: Visu Makam, Philipp Reichenbach, Anna Seigal

open_problems.why_unsolved: This is a technique-derived proof-boundary question. The source geometry makes differentiation at the identity available, but the literature does not show that equality of covariance-model tangent spaces determines the target-indexed nonsingleton partition. The first proof step that must be supplied is a support-minimality argument for the off-diagonal Jacobian columns, followed by a proof that every support of size at least two has a uniquely recoverable target even with arbitrary extra singleton and nonsingleton parents. Searches for diagonal tangent spaces or tangent-support block recovery in coloured Gaussian DAGs found the geometry papers but no reconstruction theorem.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An injectivity theorem and explicit reconstruction map from the diagonal off-diagonal tangent space to all nonsingleton parent-block families, or a smallest legal pair with equal tangent spaces and different families.

writing_exemplar.why: Its geometry-to-identifiability narrative directly motivates asking which discrete colouring information is visible in local covariance geometry.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: coefficient equalities define a smooth covariance submanifold -> its Jacobian records first-order observable restrictions -> existing arguments obtain special-case identifiability -> ask whether tangent supports recover every nonsingleton parent block

method_exemplars.technique: Differentiate the rationally invertible acyclic covariance parametrization and use the block-ordered Jacobian from the smoothness proof.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired combinatorial signature is the image of the coefficient-block coordinate directions under exactly this differential.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate compatible-colouring regression coordinates by constrained least squares and use MLE uniqueness to connect sample geometry to the population tangent object.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the closest estimation machinery for the equality-constrained coordinates whose population supports would be reconstructed.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct an exact sparse covariance separator showing that an orientation disagreement between equivalent blocked-colour states can occur only across endpoints with identical nonsingleton parent-block families, even when other arrows also differ.

source_refs.claim: Question 20 says it is unknown which coloured edges may reverse or be recoloured while preserving an edge-coloured Gaussian DAG model.
source_refs.author: Tobias Boege, Kaie Kubjas, Pratik Misra, Liam Solus
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B

source_refs.claim: Covered reversals generate ordinary Markov equivalence, but the theorem does not preserve coefficient-equality constraints.
source_refs.author: David Maxwell Chickering

open_problems.why_unsolved: Ordinary Markov equivalence controls only the skeleton and unshielded colliders, not target-indexed coefficient partitions. The first proof step that changes is to replace the covered-reversal argument by a legal source covariance with only a reversed-edge coefficient and one split block active, then compute the destination regression with arbitrary additional parents. That witness must stay positive definite, satisfy every source block equality, and violate a destination block equality without assuming that the compared DAGs differ by only one arrow. Searches for sparse covariance separators for reversed coloured edges found only the general ideal-membership machinery of Boege et al., not this local witness theorem.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A separator lemma giving an explicit positive-definite covariance witness for every reversed edge whose endpoint nonsingleton block families differ, or a legal full-model-equivalent pair disproving the restriction.

writing_exemplar.why: Its open question isolates uncertainty about which coloured edges can reverse, exactly the local obstruction a separator must resolve.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: model equality is testable through rational covariance constraints -> colours may fix more structure than conditional independence -> reversible edges are the unresolved ambiguity -> separate every forbidden reversal by one exact covariance

method_exemplars.technique: Evaluate edge-identifying rational functions and saturated colouring constraints on a deliberately sparse acyclic parametrization.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired witness must satisfy one model's rational constraints while making a destination coefficient-equality constraint fail.

method_exemplars.technique: Use rational structural-parameter recovery and explicit polynomial covariance constraints to separate SEM model images beyond conditional independence.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The separator is an algebraic distinction between two observational covariance images invisible to ordinary Markov equivalence.

open_problems.open_problem: Give a finite canonical representation, exact component count, and duplicate-free output-sensitive enumeration of every blocked-colour covariance-model equivalence component with singleton blocks.

source_refs.claim: The paper says an essential-graph and transformational characterization would enable coloured causal discovery, but it does not represent nontrivial singleton-block components.
source_refs.author: Tobias Boege, Kaie Kubjas, Pratik Misra, Liam Solus
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B

source_refs.claim: Ordinary Markov-equivalent DAGs admit linear-delay enumeration, and successive outputs can be kept within structural Hamming distance three.
source_refs.author: Marcel Wienöbst, Malte Luttermann, Max Bannach, Maciej Liśkiewicz

source_refs.claim: Ordinary MECs admit polynomial-time exact counting and uniform sampling via CPDAG chain-component structure.
source_refs.author: Marcel Wienöbst, Max Bannach, Maciej Liśkiewicz

open_problems.why_unsolved: Ordinary algorithms factor a CPDAG into chain components and enumerate acyclic moral orientations. A blocked-colour component adds vertex-specific parent partitions: an orientation is admissible only when every reversal is singleton-compatible and transports the common-parent partition correctly. The first proof step that changes is therefore the CPDAG chain-component factorization; it must be replaced or augmented by fixed nonsingleton families and compatibility constraints. Searches for BPEC-DAG or blocked-colour component counting and enumeration returned GECS and ordinary-MEC algorithms but no target-family result.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A canonical finite component object with an exact cardinality formula or recurrence and an algorithm that lists each blocked-colour state exactly once with proved polynomial delay, while also returning a minimum-length reversal path between any two members.

writing_exemplar.why: It connects equivalence-class size to causal ambiguity and turns a structural representation into exact counting and sampling tasks.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: observational data identify a class -> class size governs causal ambiguity and computation -> CPDAG structure enables exact counting -> seek the corresponding component calculus under partition constraints

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt maximum-cardinality-search enumeration and its reverse-search correctness proof to legal partition-transported reversals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It gives the sharpest output-delay result for the unconstrained MEC containing each blocked-colour component.

method_exemplars.technique: Replace CPDAG chain-component factorization and clique-tree dynamic programming by colour-compatible orientation states.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested exact cardinality is the same object with additional local partition constraints.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the monotone covered-reversal construction and its disagreement-decreasing invariant to certify path length.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A shortest-path result must show that every disagreeing edge is reversed once while all intermediate partitions remain legal.

open_problems.open_problem: Establish fixed-p generic consistency of Gaussian likelihood/BIC for recovering the true blocked-colour covariance-model equivalence component when singleton blocks create exact likelihood ties.

source_refs.claim: The paper introduces decomposable BIC scoring for GECS but explicitly leaves its consistency under faithfulness for future work.
source_refs.author: Tobias Boege, Kaie Kubjas, Pratik Misra, Liam Solus
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B

source_refs.claim: BIC-type posterior expansions consistently compare finite smooth curved submodels of an exponential family under regularity conditions.
source_refs.author: Dominique M. A. Haughton

source_refs.claim: GES consistency is obtained from local score consistency and a transformational path argument, with additional conditions for uniform high-dimensional results.
source_refs.author: Preetam Nandy, Alain Hauser, Marloes H. Maathuis

open_problems.why_unsolved: Boege et al. evaluate GECS empirically and identify coloured moves as the obstacle to a Chickering-style consistency proof. Their search class is singleton-free and hence structurally identifiable; here, equivalent labelled states have exactly tied likelihoods while nonequivalent components can intersect on lower-dimensional parameter sets. The first new step is to quotient the finite state space by full-model equivalence and prove that, away from an explicit algebraic exceptional set, every competing component of no larger dimension has positive Gaussian KL separation; a greedy version would additionally need a legal monotone score-improving path.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A fixed-p theorem that global BIC, and separately GECS if feasible, selects the true minimal blocked-colour model-equivalence component with probability tending to one under an explicit genericity condition.

writing_exemplar.why: Its causal-discovery section introduces the local coloured BIC score and ends by isolating consistency as the missing theoretical step.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: blocked coefficient equalities permit local likelihood scoring -> GECS works empirically in an identifiable subclass -> singleton blocks replace point identification by components -> prove generic recovery of the observational component

method_exemplars.technique: Apply likelihood expansions for a finite family of smooth curved exponential submodels and compare dimension penalties after quotienting exact ties.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Fixed blocked-colour covariance models are smooth finite-dimensional submanifolds, matching the regular global-BIC comparison once exceptional intersections are removed.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine local score consistency with a monotone transformational path so greedy equivalence search cannot stop before reaching the correct model.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The unresolved greedy half requires exactly a colour-compatible replacement for this GES path proof.

method_exemplars.technique: Use compatible-colouring least-squares formulas and sample-size conditions for MLE existence and uniqueness.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Blocked colourings retain targetwise likelihood decomposition even when singleton blocks induce equivalence components.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct simultaneous inference for the finite set of total causal effects induced by a recovered blocked-colour covariance-model equivalence component, including component-selection uncertainty.

source_refs.claim: IDA estimates the distinct possible total causal effects over all DAGs in an estimated ordinary Markov equivalence class.
source_refs.author: Marloes H. Maathuis, Markus Kalisch, Peter Bühlmann

source_refs.claim: The paper identifies total effects and constructs rigorous confidence regions under graph uncertainty induced by partial homoscedasticity.
source_refs.author: David Strieder, Mathias Drton

source_refs.claim: Resampling and screening give post-causal-discovery confidence sets with asymptotically correct coverage for a fixed population effect.
source_refs.author: Ting-Hsuan Chang, Zijian Guo, Daniel Malinsky

open_problems.why_unsolved: IDA treats ordinary CPDAG ambiguity, Strieder and Drton treat variance-equality structure uncertainty, and Chang et al. protect a fixed effect after constraint-based discovery. None treats the finite set indexed by coefficient-partition states that define exactly the same observational covariance model. The first proof step that changes is to replace CPDAG parent-set enumeration by the blocked reversal component and stack the smooth state-specific path-effect maps; the proof must then absorb component-selection error and remain valid when two state-specific effects coincide or their joint covariance is singular. Searches for BPEC-DAG or blocked coefficient-colour effect confidence regions found no such theorem.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An estimator of the component-indexed finite causal-effect set and a joint Gaussian, bootstrap, or test-inversion confidence region with asymptotically correct simultaneous coverage and an explicit treatment of coincident effects.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames graph identification as instrumental to the practically central target, total effects, and moves from partial structure to confidence regions.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: observational data leave structural ambiguity -> practitioners need intervention effects rather than the whole DAG -> equality restrictions shrink but may not eliminate ambiguity -> infer the complete finite effect set under blocked coefficient homogeneity

method_exemplars.technique: Enumerate valid parent-adjustment regressions and prove consistency of the resulting multiset of possible linear total effects.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target is the same finite collection of DAG-specific total effects, indexed here by a finer blocked-colour component.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert likelihood-based tests over equality-restricted Gaussian structures to obtain confidence regions for total effects.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Partial homoscedasticity creates equality-refined equivalence classes structurally analogous to coefficient-partition components.

method_exemplars.technique: Resample discovery statistics, screen candidate graphs, and union graph-specific intervals to preserve coverage after selection.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly addresses the extra coverage loss from using the same sample to select a component and estimate causal effects.

literature_map:
Boege, Kubjas, Misra & Solus (2026, JRSSB; arXiv:2404.04024) is the direct anchor: Questions 20–21 leave graphical and transformational model equivalence open when singleton or uncoloured edges are admitted.
Their edge-only generic-faithfulness result means ordinary skeleton and unshielded colliders remain necessary here, but not sufficient.
Verma & Pearl (1990, UAI) supply the ordinary skeleton-and-v-structure benchmark that coefficient equalities must refine.
Chickering (1995, UAI) supplies covered-reversal generation and one-reversal-per-disagreement paths; partition preservation is the missing step.
Chickering (2002, JMLR) proves the Meek conjecture and GES consistency through additions plus covered reversals; Boege et al. explicitly call a coloured analogue unresolved.
Andersson, Madigan & Perlman (1997, Annals of Statistics) provide the essential-graph representation motivating a canonical blocked-colour component object.
Wu & Drton (2023, IEEE JSAIT; arXiv:2308.08959) characterize equivalence under partial homoscedasticity and construct its CPDAG, the closest equality-constraint analogue.
Peters & Bühlmann (2014, Biometrika; arXiv:1205.2536) show how a global equality restriction can collapse ordinary Gaussian Markov equivalence to point identification.
Makam, Reichenbach & Seigal (2023, EJS; arXiv:2108.10058) develop compatible-colouring likelihood geometry and MLE existence and uniqueness.
Wienöbst et al. (2023, AAAI; arXiv:2301.12212) give linear-delay ordinary-MEC enumeration.
Wienöbst, Bannach & Liśkiewicz (2023, JMLR; arXiv:2205.02654) give polynomial-time ordinary-MEC counting and sampling; no blocked-colour counterpart surfaced.
Haughton (1988, Annals of Statistics) supplies regular curved-family BIC asymptotics, and Nandy, Hauser & Maathuis (2018, Annals of Statistics; arXiv:1507.02608) supply the GES consistency template.
Maathuis, Kalisch & Bühlmann (2009, Annals of Statistics; arXiv:0810.4214) estimate possible effects over ordinary MECs.
Strieder & Drton (2025; arXiv:2408.06046) give total-effect confidence regions under partial homoscedasticity, while Chang, Guo & Malinsky (2026, Biometrika; arXiv:2405.06763) give post-discovery coverage for a fixed effect.
Searches found no theorem matching blocked-singleton equivalence, its tangent or separator lemmas, blocked-component enumeration, generic BIC component recovery, or simultaneous inference for its finite effect set.
